about: Defaults for 'Making cells: China vs India' on the Cost calculator page. Materials come live from the main cost model (costmodel.json and today's prices). Everything here is the cost of running the factory. US$ unless marked. Change a default only with a new source; values marked assumption have no direct public source and are explained in their note.

fields.label: Investment per GWh of yearly capacity
fields.china_note: EVE Energy's four new storage-cell plants announced in March–April 2026: about US$15 million per GWh (converted).
fields.india_note: Announced Indian plants: Amara Raja ₹9,500 crore for 16 GWh (about ₹594 crore per GWh) and Tata's Agratas ₹13,000 crore for 20 GWh (₹650 crore per GWh); about US$65 million per GWh on average. Exide's first 6 GWh phase is ₹5,000 crore including pack lines. The ACC PLI scheme's minimum is ₹225 crore per GWh.

fields.label: Years to pay back the plant
fields.china_note: Assumption: equipment paid back over 10 years, the same in both countries.
fields.india_note: Assumption: equipment paid back over 10 years, the same in both countries.

fields.label: Interest rate
fields.china_note: China's 5-year loan prime rate, unchanged at 3.5% in October 2026.
fields.india_note: SBI's one-year MCLR, 8.70% (from July 2026). Large borrowers may pay less, new ventures more.

fields.label: How full the plant runs
fields.china_note: CATL ran at about 65% in H1 2024 and close to 90% later; 80% sits between. Many smaller Chinese makers run far emptier.
fields.india_note: Assumption: a new Indian plant in its first years, still filling its order book.

fields.label: Good cells out of every 100 made
fields.china_note: China's leaders run at 95% or more (CRU's Aaron Wade); SMM's cell cost model also uses 95%.
fields.india_note: Assumption for a plant past its ramp-up. New plants outside China start far lower, around 50% (CRU, via EV inFocus).

fields.label: Electricity to make 1 kWh of cells
fields.china_note: Cell factories use 20–40 kWh of energy per kWh of cells, depending on the cell (Fraunhofer FFB / Nature Energy study). 25 kWh is used for large LFP cells.
fields.india_note: Same as China: the process is the same.

fields.label: Industrial power price
fields.china_note: Average industrial power price in China, about US$0.088/kWh (2024). Large-industry rates in Jiangsu and Fujian were similar in May 2025.
fields.india_note: Gujarat high-tension industry pays about ₹7.50–8.50 per unit all-in (FY2026-27); ₹8 is used (about US$0.084).

fields.label: Factory workers per GWh
fields.china_note: A mature cell plant needs about 130 direct workers per GWh of yearly output (Volta Foundation, July 2026).
fields.india_note: Same benchmark; a less automated Indian line could need more.

fields.label: Pay per worker
fields.china_note: Average manufacturing wage in China's urban non-private units, 2025 (National Bureau of Statistics), about US$17,040.
fields.china_source: National Bureau of Statistics of China
fields.india_note: Directly employed factory workers earned ₹586 a day in 2021-22 (Annual Survey of Industries); × 300 working days ≈ ₹1.76 lakh a year (about US$1,846). Skilled battery-line staff will cost more.

fields.label: Shipping cell materials in
fields.india_note: Assumption: India makes little cathode, anode or electrolyte yet, so materials are shipped from China at about the same US$1/kWh as finished cells (see Landed in India).

fields.label: Duty on imported cell materials
fields.india_note: Not confirmed: Budget 2025 removed duty on 35 capital goods for battery making and on battery scrap, but no public source gives the rate for cathode, anode, electrolyte or separator. Enter the rate from your tariff line.

pli.note: ACC PLI incentive = subsidy rate per kWh × share of value added in India × kWh sold, paid over five years once value addition reaches 25% (60% needed within five years). The rate per kWh is set by each bid, so it starts at zero here; enter a rate to see its effect.

types.label: Sodium-ion storage cell
types.note: Mysteel puts the cost of a sodium-ion (NFPP) storage cell at 0.45 against 0.342 for LFP per Wh (Aug 2026): about 32% more, mostly because sodium-ion lines are small and run about 30% full across the industry. This is applied to the modelled LFP cost, so sodium-ion here is a reference figure, not built up from its own materials.

recipe_note: All three LFP cells use one materials recipe (SMM's 314 Ah model at today's prices). Larger cells save some case and assembly cost and EV cells use thinner electrodes, but no public source puts numbers on either, so the LFP types differ here only in the market price they are compared with.

smm_check.label: SMM's China manufacturing cost
smm_check.source: SMM 314 Ah cell cost model, Mar 2026

left_out: Not included: maintenance, plant overheads, R&D, sales costs and the maker's profit. So these are costs to make, not selling prices.
